title: Can't see your device?
retrying: Asked the phone again — check its screen
stillStuck: Still stuck? Copy a diagnostic report to paste into an issue.

headline.okEmpty: No problems found — plug in a phone and it will show up
headline.allGood: Tether re-checks whenever a device appears or disappears.
headline.fixFirst: Fix the red item first — the others usually resolve on their own.

server_conflict.restarts: Another adb keeps restarting the server
server_conflict.mismatch: Two different adb versions are fighting for the server

usb_visible.none: The computer doesn't see a phone on USB

usb_debugging.off: The phone is connected, but USB debugging is off
usb_debugging.some_off: One phone on USB isn't visible to adb

usb_mode.charging: The phone may be in “Charging only” mode

authorization.pending: The phone is waiting for you to allow this computer

permissions.denied: Linux blocks access to the phone

other.title: adb server is running
other.desc: Version {{version}} on <m>{{address}}</m>, started by another tool {{uptime}}. Tether shares it.

down.title: adb server isn't running
down.desc: Nothing answers on port {{port}}. Tether retries every few seconds; restart it if this persists.

restarts.title: Another adb is fighting for the server
restarts.desc: The server restarted {{count}} times in the last minute. Devices may flicker between online and offline. Server binary: <m>{{serverBinary}}</m>.

mismatch.title: Another adb is fighting for the server
mismatch.desc: The running server speaks version {{serverVersion}}, Tether's adb ({{ours}}) speaks {{clientVersion}}. Each kills the other's server. Use one adb everywhere.

foreign.title: Server shared with another adb
foreign.desc: It was started by <m>{{serverBinary}}</m>. Same version, so they get along.

unknown.title: Server conflicts
unknown.desc: Can't tell while the server is down.

none.title: No other adb is interfering
none.desc: The server and Tether use the same adb version.

found.title: The computer sees a USB device

adb_only.title: The computer sees a USB device
adb_only.desc: adb lists a phone on USB.

none.title: No phone on USB
none.desc: The computer doesn't see an Android phone. Check that it's plugged in and unlocked, then try another cable or port.

unsupported.title: USB devices
unsupported.desc: Tether can't list USB devices on this OS yet.

ok.title: The cable carries data
ok.desc: The phone enumerates over USB, so it isn't a charge-only cable.

unknown.title: Data cable
unknown.desc: Charge-only cables are common: if nothing shows up, try another one.

off.title: USB debugging is off on the phone
off.desc: The phone doesn't expose an adb interface. Open Settings › System › Developer options and turn on USB debugging. No Developer options? Tap Build number 7 times first.

some_off.title: {{product}} isn't visible to adb
some_off.desc: Another phone works, but this one has USB debugging off.

on.title: USB debugging is on
on.desc: adb sees every phone that's plugged in.

charging.title: USB mode may be “Charging only”
charging.desc: Some phones hide debugging in this mode. Pull down notifications, tap USB charging this device and pick File transfer.

pending.title: Approve this computer on the phone
pending.desc: {{devices}} waits for “Allow USB debugging?”. Unlock it, check Always allow and tap Allow.

some.title: A device is offline
some.desc: {{devices}} stopped answering. Replug it or turn Wireless debugging off and on.

denied.title: No permission to open the phone
denied.desc: {{devices}}: Linux needs a udev rule so your user may access the phone.

ok.title: No permission problems
ok.desc: No device is blocked by permissions.

ok_macos.title: No permission problems
ok_macos.desc: macOS doesn't need USB drivers or udev rules.

not_needed.title: Windows USB driver · Linux udev rules

udev_ok.title: Android udev rules are installed
udev_ok.desc: Your user can open Android phones without root.

udev_missing.title: Android udev rules are missing
udev_missing.desc: Without them phones show up as “no permissions”. Install <m>android-udev-rules</m> or add a rule.

windows_ok.title: USB driver works
windows_ok.desc: adb talks to a phone over USB.

windows_unknown.title: Windows USB driver
windows_unknown.desc: If Device Manager shows the phone without “ADB Interface”, install the Google USB driver or your phone maker's driver.

ok.title: Wi-Fi discovery works
ok.desc: adb finds phones with Wireless debugging on the network (<m>{{version}}</m>).

off.title: Wi-Fi discovery is unavailable
off.desc: This adb has mDNS disabled; pair by IP and port instead.

unknown.title: Wi-Fi discovery
unknown.desc: Can't tell while the server is down.

restart.title: Restart the adb server?
restart.text: Tether kills the running server and starts it with its own adb. Android Studio and other tools reconnect by themselves; running transfers are interrupted.
